_comment: Landing page composition. Each entry is one block: turn it off with
published:false, move it with order, change its copy in config. Adding a new
block type is a new entry here plus a component in the registry at
components/sections/registry.tsx — the page itself never changes.
ORDER IS MEDIA-FIRST. The visitor meets the hero, then FOOTAGE, then
SCREENSHOTS, and only then reads about the game. That is the order a game
presentation uses; leading with prose is the marketing-funnel order the
brief rules out. Development status rides in the hero's status line rather
than as its own section.
COPY STATUS: anything containing the word PLACEHOLDER is NOT RENDERED — see
lib/content/placeholder.ts. So a section with unwritten copy shows less
rather than showing an instruction to the site's owner. The inventory of
what is still needed is docs/CONTENT_REQUIRED.md. No release date,
platform, price, store page or player claim is asserted anywhere.

config.title: THE KANJO
config.subtitle: NIGHT HIGHWAY RACING
config.description: An elevated expressway loop after dark, drawing on Japanese highway racing culture and the atmosphere of late 1990s and early 2000s Japan.

_README: HERO MEDIA. The canon's own composition is media + dim + UI
(UI_Canon/Screens/MainMenu/layout.json defaultTreatment.mode = 'dim').
kind is 'none' only because no footage exists yet. The hero already
reserves the full media footprint and applies the dim, so switching is a
CONTENT change with no layout change and no component edit.
A STILL — copy the export to public/media/hero/, then:
"kind": "image",
"image": { "src": "/media/hero/hero.jpg", "alt": "",
"treatment": "dim"
A LOOP — MP4 always, WebM as well if you can. A poster is MANDATORY:
it is the first paint, the fallback if the loop cannot play, and what
shows under prefers-reduced-motion, where the video is not rendered.
"kind": "video",
"videoSources": ["/media/hero/loop.webm", "/media/hero/loop.mp4"],
"poster": { "src": "/media/hero/loop-poster.jpg", "alt": "",
"treatment": "dim"
FRAMING. The hero is the only surface that crops media to an arbitrary
box, so it is the only one that needs framing control. objectPosition is
a plain CSS object-position: 'center 35%' pulls the crop upward,
'center 70%' downward, '70% center' rightward. mobileObjectPosition
applies below 768px, where the crop is tallest and a subject framed to
one side is most likely to be lost. Both default to 'center'.
mobileImage is optional and only worth supplying when the desktop frame
cannot survive a portrait crop at all — usually the mobile framing string
is enough on its own.
treatment: 'dim' (canon default) | 'strong_dim' | 'transparent' |
'blackout'. Use strong_dim if a bright capture makes the title hard to
read; the canon's rule is to preserve UI contrast over variable imagery.
See docs/MEDIA_WORKFLOW.md for resolution, safe composition area,
duration, codec, file size and whether to strip audio.

config.heading: ONE LOOP, AFTER DARK
config.body:
The Kanjo is a racing game built around a single elevated expressway loop at night — a fictionalised Japanese night circuit, loosely inspired rather than reproduced.

Handling aims at believable vehicle behaviour rather than simulation for its own sake, and the interface stays deliberately minimal: the road, the traffic, and the car.
